inline.s: When I was thirty-five, I already knew that the post-heavenly world had reached its final decline, and that in time it would become the pre-heavenly world! How then do the pre-heavenly and the post-heavenly differ? Everyone who cares only for his wife and children belongs to the post-heavenly; whoever disregards home and family and seeks only the common good belongs to the pre-heavenly. When I was twenty-one and working as a hired laborer, I saw some brothers dividing up the family estate, taking up knives and guns over the inheritance, and there were even cases that ended in loss of life. I wondered to myself, for whom were they contending? I thought about it for a whole day, and then suddenly I understood: they were contending for their wives and sons! At that moment I was carrying dung, and I threw the dung basket onto the pile and said loudly, 'I must become an extraordinary person!' My companions stared at me, not knowing what I meant. When I reached thirty-eight and was keeping vigil at the grave, I said to the women of the family, 'From now on I can no longer run the household for you.' When the period of grave-keeping came to an end, I took exhorting people to goodness and establishing learning as my life's calling, and I have done so up to the present day.

When the Meng family of Mengjiatun in Jinxi County rebuilt the Temple of Mother Meng, the undertaking was enormous. Upon its completion I went to visit and met Meng Laofeng, the temple's manager. I made him a deep bow, but he paid me no attention; I spoke to him, but he gave no answer. As I walked out of the temple I made a vow: 'So the Meng family produced a sage, and you are so arrogant! May the Wang family not also produce a sage? I must resolve to learn to become a sage!' A bystander jeered at me, saying, 'Can you ever catch up to her?' I replied, 'Even if I cannot catch up, I will walk a few steps after her!'

I heard someone explain that the Doctrine of the Mean says, 'Filial piety consists in well carrying on the aims of one's fathers and well setting forth their deeds.' That is spoken of one's own forebears, but I think it can be extended further. I heard the story of 'Yang Jiao'ai giving up his life to fully preserve friendship,' and so I carried on Yang Jiao'ai's aim and went to rescue the good person Yang Bai, thereby also setting forth Yang Jiao'ai's deed. In doing this I turned from ignorance to clarity. Whose aim among the sages and worthies may one not carry on? Whoever carries on the aim of a sage or worthy — is he not a 'filial son'?

In the world today, all the gods and spirits are present among human beings, yet they have not been born again and descended into the world. Whose aim you seize, that one's spiritual radiance comes to you; whichever deity you emulate, that deity's spirit arrives; whichever sage or worthy you emulate, that sage or worthy's spirit arrives. Whatever matter you meet, learn from the one who embodies it — like picking flowers: pluck one, do one. Mencius said, 'Every person can become Yao or Shun'; this is precisely to bid people seize an aim. If an ordinary person never seizes the aim of the ancients, he remains an ordinary person to the end.
